+## HiSparse decoding (experimental)
+

+{
+  "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",

+  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+    "connectors": [

+      {"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Set `host_pool_gib` to the host-cache capacity in GiB per data-parallel replica.
+The prefiller and decoder can use different TP sizes, such as TP2 and TP4.

@@ -480,4 +480,17 @@ vllm serve model --enable-lora --lora-target-modules o_proj
 vllm serve model --enable-lora --lora-target-modules o_proj qkv_proj down_proj
 ```
 
-When `--lora-target-modules` is not specified, LoRA will be applied to all supported modules in the model. This parameter accepts module suffixes (the last component of the module name), such as `o_proj`, `qkv_proj`, `gate_proj`, etc.
+`--lora-target-modules` is an explicit allowlist for module names or suffixes such as `o_proj`, `qkv_proj`, and `gate_proj`. When set, this list takes precedence over `--enable-lora-embedding-modules`.
+
+### Embedding Modules
+
+By default, LoRA skips embedding modules (input embeddings and `lm_head`), so vLLM allocates no LoRA buffers for them.
+Use `--enable-lora-embedding-modules` to enable both alongside the default modules. The Python `LLM` argument is `enable_lora_embedding_modules=True`.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve model --enable-lora --enable-lora-embedding-modules
+```
+
+If an adapter contains weights for an embedding module excluded by default, vLLM logs a warning, skips those weights, and applies the remaining enabled weights. Use an explicit `--lora-target-modules` list for finer control, such as enabling input embedding LoRA without `lm_head`.
+
+Enabling `lm_head` LoRA through either option disables prompt scoring for the deployment. Requests using `prompt_logprobs` (including `0`) or `prompt_logprob_token_ids` receive a validation error. This restriction also applies to base-model requests because they can be batched with LoRA requests. Input embedding LoRA supports prompt scoring when `lm_head` LoRA is disabled.

@@ -150,6 +150,25 @@ Kimi-K3 on MI355X supports specialized decode on built-in MoRIIO READ and WRITE
 
 Use matching transfer modes and cache layouts. See [supported deployments](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/README.md#supported-deployments) for the hardware, state dtype, and execution requirements.
 
+### Attention cache layouts
+
+MoRIIO supports standardized 4D attention caches whose scheduler blocks are
+split into smaller kernel blocks. For example, AITER FA can use 32-token kernel
+blocks with `--block-size 64` and `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=0` on both
+servers. The connector transfers each
+complete scheduler block, including all of its kernel blocks. Both peers must
+use matching kernel-block layouts. Split blocks must form non-overlapping,
+contiguous scheduler pages; incomplete groups are
+rejected. This grouping supports equal-TP transfers; split layouts that cannot
+be sliced by head remain unsupported between different TP sizes.
+
+For AITER FA with `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`, MoRIIO transfers the
+separate dense K/V planes in READ and WRITE mode. Use the same backend, KV dtype,
+shuffle setting, block size, and TP size on both servers. Blocks must not be split
+into smaller kernel blocks; the tested Qwen3 BF16 configuration uses
+`--block-size 16`.
+These packed planes do not support transfers between different TP sizes.
+
 ### Different prefill and decode TP sizes
 
 In WRITE mode, the prefill and decode instances can use different tensor-parallel sizes, as long as one is a multiple of the other. Each prefill rank writes its shard into the decode ranks that hold it:

@@ -191,6 +191,61 @@ With `return_token_ids`, the response carries `mm_hashes` next to `mm_placeholde
 - The processor cache is disabled (`--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`), so the returned keys can't be reused.
 - The server runs the Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) which doesn't support omitting `kwargs_data` yet. It still returns `mm_hashes`.
 
+### Processed tensors in object storage
+
+A client that already has an item's processed tensors, such as an RL trainer on another node, can upload them to an S3-compatible store and send a reference in `features.kwargs_refs` instead of inlining them in `kwargs_data`. The tensors then skip the request body and any gateway in front of vLLM. The server downloads each object, checks its size and SHA-256 digest, and rebuilds the model's field metadata before it submits the request to the engine.
+
+Each object holds one item, saved with `safetensors.torch.save`. Its tensors are the ones this server's multimodal processor produces for that item, under the same names and dtypes and with their batch dimension, so the same tensors that `/render` returns in `kwargs_data`. The client doesn't need vLLM, but the tensors can differ from what the model's Hugging Face processor returns. For example, Qwen3-VL with the default `mm_device_do_normalize` normalizes on the GPU, so its object holds a `uint8` `pixel_values` and an `image_grid_thw` of shape `[1, 3]`:
+
+```python
+import hashlib
+
+import boto3
+from safetensors.torch import save
+
+payload = save({"pixel_values": pixel_values, "image_grid_thw": image_grid_thw})
+key = f"rollouts/{request_id}/image-0"
+boto3.client("s3").put_object(Bucket="mm-tensors", Key=key, Body=payload)
+
+features = {
+    "mm_hashes": {"image": [image_hash]},
+    "mm_placeholders": {"image": [{"offset": 15, "length": 64}]},
+    "kwargs_refs": {
+        "image": [{
+            "uri": f"s3://mm-tensors/{key}",
+            "format": "safetensors-v1",
+            "nbytes": len(payload),
+            "digest": hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
+        }]
+    },
+}
+```
+
+Like `kwargs_data`, each `kwargs_refs` list is parallel to `mm_hashes`, and a `null` entry falls back to `kwargs_data` or the processor cache. An item can't set both. `mm_metadata` for a referenced item may only repeat fields of its object with the same values. The `mm_hashes` entry stays the cache key, so give different content different hashes.
+
+`kwargs_refs` are off by default. Enable them at startup with `--mm-tensor-refs-config`; a server started without it rejects them with a 400:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct --enable-scale-out \
+    --mm-tensor-refs-config '{"s3_allowed_uri_prefix": "s3://mm-tensors/rollouts"}'
+```
+
+The config's fields are:
+
+- `s3_allowed_uri_prefix`: the `s3://bucket/prefix` that every reference must be under. Required.
+- `max_object_bytes`: the largest object the server downloads. Default: 1 GiB.
+- `max_request_bytes`: the largest total size of the objects one request references. A request over it fails with a 400 before anything is downloaded. Default: 1 GiB.
+- `max_reserved_bytes`: the memory one API server reserves for referenced tensors. Each request reserves twice the declared size of its objects, for the downloaded bytes and the decoded tensors, and keeps the reservation until it finishes, even if the client disconnects. Requests wait in arrival order until their reservation fits. It must be at least twice `max_request_bytes`. Default: 8 GiB.
+- `max_concurrent_reads`: how many requests per API server can download references at once. Default: 32.
+
+The endpoint and credentials come from the server's environment, never from the request: `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` if set, otherwise the standard boto3 configuration (for example `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3`, or `addressing_style` in the AWS config file). The server needs `boto3` installed, creates its S3 client at startup, and never deletes objects, so expire them on the client side, for example with a bucket lifecycle rule. Only the Python frontend accepts `kwargs_refs`.
+
+Like `kwargs_data`, `kwargs_refs` is meant for clients in one trust domain:
+
+- The server reads objects with its own credentials, so every caller of the endpoint can reference every object the server can read under the allowed prefix. Don't share a prefix between callers that shouldn't see each other's objects.
+- A missing, inaccessible or mismatched object (wrong size or digest) returns the same 422, so a caller can't probe objects it doesn't know. The details are in the server log.
+- The server checks each object's size, digest and fields, but tensors with a shape the model doesn't expect, such as `pixel_values` rows of the wrong width, can still fail inside the engine.
+
 ## Aborting requests
 
 `POST /inference/v1/abort_requests` aborts in-flight requests. It is registered wherever `/inference/v1/generate` is and requires the API key when `--api-key` is set, like `/inference/v1/generate`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for client-processed multimodal tensors loaded from S3."""
+
+import asyncio
+import gc
+import hashlib
+import io
+import threading
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from botocore.exceptions import ClientError
+from safetensors.torch import save as save_safetensors
+
+from vllm.config.mm_tensor_refs import MMTensorRefsConfig
+from vllm.exceptions import RetryableRequestError
+from vllm.multimodal import s3_transport
+from vllm.multimodal.s3_transport import (
+    S3MMReader,
+    S3MMReference,
+)
+from vllm.multimodal.tensor_transport import (
+    MMTensorMemoryBudget,
+    MMTensorTransportError,
+    ReleasingStream,
+    run_in_read_slot,
+    validate_mm_tensor_request_size,
+)
+from vllm.utils.import_utils import PlaceholderModule
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+URI = "s3://tensor-bucket/tenant/mm/request/image-0"
+
+
+class FakeBody(io.BytesIO):
+    def __init__(self, payload: bytes):
+        super().__init__(payload)
+        self.read_sizes: list[int | None] = []
+
+    def read(self, size: int | None = -1) -> bytes:
+        self.read_sizes.append(size)
+        return super().read(size)
+
+
+class FakeS3Client:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        payload: bytes | None,
+        content_length: int | None = None,
+        error: Exception | None = None,
+    ):
+        self.body = None if payload is None else FakeBody(payload)
+        self.content_length = content_length
+        self.error = error
+        self.calls: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+
+    def get_object(self, **kwargs):
+        self.calls.append(kwargs)
+        if self.error is not None:
+            raise self.error
+        return {"Body": self.body, "ContentLength": self.content_length}
+
+
+def _tensors() -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    return {
+        "pixel_values": torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(3, 4),
+        "num_patches": torch.tensor([3], dtype=torch.int64),
+    }
+
+
+def _reference(
+    payload: bytes,
+    *,
+    uri: str = URI,
+    nbytes: int | None = None,
+    digest: str | None = None,
+) -> S3MMReference:
+    return S3MMReference(
+        uri=uri,
+        format="safetensors-v1",
+        nbytes=len(payload) if nbytes is None else nbytes,
+        digest=hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() if digest is None else digest,
+    )
+
+
+CONFIG = MMTensorRefsConfig(
+    s3_allowed_uri_prefix="s3://tensor-bucket/tenant/mm",
+    max_object_bytes=1024**2,
+    max_request_bytes=3 * 1024**2,
+    max_reserved_bytes=6 * 1024**2,
+)
+
+
+def _reader(client=None, config=CONFIG) -> S3MMReader:
+    return S3MMReader(config, object() if client is None else client)
+
+
+def test_reader_reads_at_most_declared_size_and_decodes():
+    expected = _tensors()
+    payload = save_safetensors(expected)
+    client = FakeS3Client(payload, content_length=len(payload))
+
+    tensors = _reader(client).read(_reference(payload))
+
+    assert client.calls == [
+        {"Bucket": "tensor-bucket", "Key": "tenant/mm/request/image-0"}
+    ]
+    assert client.body is not None
+    assert client.body.read_sizes == [len(payload) + 1]
+    assert client.body.closed
+    assert tensors.keys() == expected.keys()
+    assert all(torch.equal(tensors[k], v) for k, v in expected.items())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "uri",
+    [
+        "s3://other-bucket/tenant/mm/request/image-0",
+        "s3://tensor-bucket/other/request/image-0",
+        "s3://tensor-bucket/tenant/mm-elsewhere/image-0",
+        "s3://tensor-bucket/tenant/mm/../other/image-0",
+        "https://tensor-bucket/tenant/mm/request/image-0",
+    ],
+)
+def test_reference_outside_allowed_prefix_is_rejected(uri):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="configured prefix|Invalid S3 URI"):
+        _reader().validate(_reference(b"x", uri=uri))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("fields", "match"),
+    [
+        ({}, "s3_allowed_uri_prefix must be set"),
+        ({"s3_allowed_uri_prefix": "tensor-bucket/mm"}, "s3_allowed_uri_prefix"),
+        (
+            {"s3_allowed_uri_prefix": "s3://b/p", "max_reserved_bytes": 2**30},
+            "at least twice max_request_bytes",
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_config_rejects_bad_settings(fields, match):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=match):
+        MMTensorRefsConfig(**fields)
+
+
+def test_bucket_only_prefix_allows_any_key():
+    config = MMTensorRefsConfig(s3_allowed_uri_prefix="s3://tensor-bucket")
+
+    assert _reader(config=config).validate(_reference(b"x", uri=URI)) == (
+        "tensor-bucket",
+        "tenant/mm/request/image-0",
+    )
+
+
+def test_reference_over_size_limit_is_rejected():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="configured limit"):
+        _reader().validate(_reference(b"x", nbytes=1024**2 + 1))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("status", "code", "expected"),
+    [
+        (404, "NoSuchKey", MMTensorTransportError),
+        (503, "SlowDown", RetryableRequestError),
+    ],
+)
+def test_reader_maps_store_errors_by_status(status, code, expected):
+    error = ClientError(
+        {"Error": {"Code": code}, "ResponseMetadata": {"HTTPStatusCode": status}},
+        "GetObject",
+    )
+    reader = _reader(FakeS3Client(None, error=error))
+
+    with pytest.raises(expected, match="Could not load"):
+        reader.read(_reference(b"x"))
+
+
+UNAVAILABLE = f"Could not load multimodal tensor object '{URI}'"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("served", "content_length", "digest"),
+    [
+        ("missing", None, None),
+        ("payload", None, None),
+        ("payload", 1, None),
+        ("short", "declared", None),
+        ("long", "declared", None),
+        ("payload", "declared", "0" * 64),
+    ],
+)
+def test_reader_errors_dont_reveal_the_object(served, content_length, digest):
+    """Missing and mismatched objects fail alike, without their size or status."""
+    payload = save_safetensors(_tensors())
+    body = {"payload": payload, "short": payload[:-1], "long": payload + b"x"}
+    if served == "missing":
+        error = ClientError(
+            {
+                "Error": {"Code": "NoSuchKey"},
+                "ResponseMetadata": {"HTTPStatusCode": 404},
+            },
+            "GetObject",
+        )
+        client = FakeS3Client(None, error=error)
+    else:
+        length = len(payload) if content_length == "declared" else content_length
+        client = FakeS3Client(body[served], content_length=length)
+
+    with pytest.raises(MMTensorTransportError) as excinfo:
+        _reader(client).read(_reference(payload, digest=digest))
+
+    assert str(excinfo.value) == UNAVAILABLE
+    if client.body is not None:
+        assert client.body.closed
+
+
+def test_reader_without_boto3_fails_at_startup_not_per_request(monkeypatch):
+    """Without boto3, a bad reference is still a 400; only the client needs it."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(s3_transport, "boto3", PlaceholderModule("boto3_missing"))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(s3_transport, "botocore", PlaceholderModule("botocore_missing"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="configured prefix"):
+        _reader().read(_reference(b"x", uri="s3://other-bucket/k"))
+    with pytest.raises(ImportError):
+        S3MMReader(CONFIG)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("payload", "match"),
+    [
+        (b"not safetensors", "Could not decode"),
+        (save_safetensors({}), "contains no tensors"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_reader_rejects_bad_payload(payload, match):
+    client = FakeS3Client(payload, content_length=len(payload))
+
+    with pytest.raises(MMTensorTransportError, match=match):
+        _reader(client).read(_reference(payload))
+
+
+def test_request_size_limit_counts_every_reference():
+    references = [_reference(b"x", nbytes=1024**2) for _ in range(3)]
+    assert validate_mm_tensor_request_size(references, 3 * 1024**2) == 3 * 1024**2
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="in one request declare 4194304 bytes"):
+        validate_mm_tensor_request_size([*references, references[0]], 3 * 1024**2)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_cancelled_read_keeps_its_slot_until_the_read_finishes():
+    """A client disconnect cancels the request, but not the executor thread."""
+    slots = asyncio.Semaphore(1)
+    unblock = threading.Event()
+    started: list[str] = []
+
+    def blocked_read() -> str:
+        started.append("first")
+        unblock.wait(timeout=30)
+        return "first"
+
+    def next_read() -> str:
+        started.append("second")
+        return "second"
+
+    first = asyncio.create_task(run_in_read_slot(slots, blocked_read))
+    async with asyncio.timeout(10):
+        while not started:
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
+    first.cancel()
+    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+        await first
+    # Still held by the cancelled read, before anyone else asks for it.
+    assert slots.locked()
+
+    second = asyncio.create_task(run_in_read_slot(slots, next_read))
+    await asyncio.sleep(0)
+    assert not second.done()
+    assert started == ["first"]
+
+    unblock.set()
+    async with asyncio.timeout(10):
+        assert await second == "second"
+    assert started == ["first", "second"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_memory_budget_waits_in_order_and_survives_cancellation():
+    budget = MMTensorMemoryBudget(100)
+    first = await budget.reserve(60)
+
+    cancelled = asyncio.create_task(budget.reserve(50))
+    queued = asyncio.create_task(budget.reserve(40))
+    await asyncio.sleep(0)
+    assert not cancelled.done() and not queued.done()
+
+    # The waiter at the head leaves; the next one fits and gets its bytes.
+    cancelled.cancel()
+    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+        await cancelled
+    second = await asyncio.wait_for(queued, timeout=10)
+    assert budget.used_nbytes == 100
+
+    first.release()
+    second.release()
+    assert budget.used_nbytes == 0
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_reserved_bytes"):
+        await budget.reserve(101)
+
+

+async def test_reservation_outlives_a_cancelled_read():
+    """The read thread keeps its bytes after the request lets go of them."""
+    budget = MMTensorMemoryBudget(100)

+
+

+

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from pydantic import Field, model_validator
+
+from vllm.config.utils import config
+
+
+@config
+class MMTensorRefsConfig:
+    """Configuration for `features.kwargs_refs` in `/inference/v1/generate`:
+    processed multimodal tensors that clients upload to an S3-compatible store
+    and reference by URI. Passing this config enables them."""
+
+    s3_allowed_uri_prefix: str = ""
+    """The `s3://bucket/prefix` that every reference must be under. Required.
+    Every caller of the endpoint can reference every object the server can
+    read under it, so use one prefix per trust domain."""
+
+    max_object_bytes: int = Field(default=1 << 30, gt=0)
+    """The largest object the server downloads. Default: 1 GiB."""
+
+    max_request_bytes: int = Field(default=1 << 30, gt=0)
+    """The largest total size of the objects one request references. A request
+    over it fails with a 400 before anything is downloaded. Default: 1 GiB."""
+
+    max_reserved_bytes: int = Field(default=8 << 30, gt=0)
+    """The memory one API server reserves for referenced tensors. Each request
+    reserves twice the declared size of its objects, for the downloaded bytes
+    and the decoded tensors, and keeps the reservation until it finishes, even
+    if the client disconnects. Requests wait in arrival order until their
+    reservation fits. Must be at least twice `max_request_bytes`.
+    Default: 8 GiB."""
+
+    max_concurrent_reads: int = Field(default=32, ge=1)
+    """How many requests per API server can download references at once.

+class S3MMReference(BaseMMTensorReference):
+    """Reference to one processed multimodal tensor bundle in S3."""
+
+    uri: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2048)
+    """An `s3://bucket/key` URI under the configured `s3_allowed_uri_prefix`."""
+
+
+def _parse_s3_uri(uri: str, *, allow_empty_key: bool = False) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    parsed = urlsplit(uri)
+    key = parsed.path.removeprefix("/")
+    if (
+        parsed.scheme.lower() != "s3"
+        or not parsed.netloc
+        or (not key and not allow_empty_key)
+        or parsed.query
+        or parsed.fragment
+        or any(part in (".", "..") for part in key.split("/"))
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid S3 URI {uri!r}; expected s3://bucket/key")
+    return parsed.netloc, key
+
+

+    """Load client-provided multimodal tensors from an S3-compatible store.
+

+    if set, otherwise the standard boto3 configuration. Every caller of the

+        self._max_object_bytes = config.max_object_bytes

+                "s3",
+                endpoint_url=envs.S3_ENDPOINT_URL,
+                config=botocore.config.Config(
+                    max_pool_connections=max(10, config.max_concurrent_reads)
+                ),
+            )

+    def validate(self, reference: S3MMReference) -> tuple[str, str]:
+        """Validate a reference and return its server-approved bucket and key."""
+        bucket, key = _parse_s3_uri(reference.uri)
+        if bucket != self._allowed_bucket or (
+            self._allowed_key and not key.startswith(f"{self._allowed_key}/")
+        ):

+
+    def read(self, reference: S3MMReference) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Fetch, bound, verify, and decode one referenced tensor bundle.
+
+        A missing, inaccessible or mismatched object raises the same error, so
+        a caller can't learn about objects it doesn't already know.
+
+        Raises:
+            ValueError: If the reference is not allowed.
+            MMTensorTransportError: If the object can't be loaded or decoded.
+            RetryableRequestError: If the store failed or was unreachable.
+
+        """
+        bucket, key = self.validate(reference)
+
+        def unavailable(detail: str) -> MMTensorTransportError:
+            logger.info("Could not load %r: %s", reference.uri, detail)
+            return MMTensorTransportError(
+                f"Could not load multimodal tensor object {reference.uri!r}"
+            )
+
+        try:
+            response = self._s3_client.get_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key)
+        except botocore.exceptions.ClientError as e:
+            status = e.response.get("ResponseMetadata", {}).get("HTTPStatusCode")
+            if status is not None and status < 500 and status not in (408, 429):
+                raise unavailable(f"HTTP {status}") from e
+            raise RetryableRequestError(
+                f"Could not load multimodal tensor object {reference.uri!r}"
+            ) from e
+        except botocore.exceptions.BotoCoreError as e:
+            raise RetryableRequestError(
+                f"Could not load multimodal tensor object {reference.uri!r}"
+            ) from e
+
+        body = response.get("Body")
+        if body is None:
+            raise unavailable("response has no body")
+
+        try:
+            with contextlib.closing(body):
+                content_length = response.get("ContentLength")
+                if content_length != reference.nbytes:
+                    raise unavailable(
+                        f"object has {content_length} bytes, "
+                        f"reference declares {reference.nbytes}"
+                    )
+                payload = body.read(reference.nbytes + 1)
+        except (botocore.exceptions.BotoCoreError, OSError) as e:
+            raise RetryableRequestError(
+                f"Could not read multimodal tensor object {reference.uri!r}"
+            ) from e
+
+        if len(payload) != reference.nbytes:
+            raise unavailable(
+                f"read {len(payload)} bytes, reference declares {reference.nbytes}"
+            )
+        if not verify_mm_tensor_digest(payload, reference.digest):
+            raise unavailable("SHA-256 digest mismatch")
+        return decode_mm_tensor_bundle(payload, location=repr(reference.uri))

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Shared contracts for externally stored multimodal tensor bundles."""
+
+import asyncio
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import weakref
+from collections import deque
+from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, AsyncIterator, Callable, Iterable
+from concurrent.futures import Executor
+from typing import Literal, TypeVar
+
+import torch
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
+from safetensors.torch import load as load_safetensors
+
+from vllm.exceptions import VLLMUnprocessableEntityError
+
+MM_TENSOR_FORMAT = "safetensors-v1"
+
+_T = TypeVar("_T")
+
+
+class BaseMMTensorReference(BaseModel):
+    """Common metadata for one externally stored tensor bundle."""
+
+    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
+
+    format: Literal["safetensors-v1"]
+    nbytes: int = Field(gt=0)
+    digest: str = Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
+    """Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the object bytes."""
+
+
+class MMTensorTransportError(VLLMUnprocessableEntityError):
+    """Raised when an external multimodal tensor bundle cannot be used."""
+
+
+def validate_mm_tensor_request_size(
+    references: Iterable[BaseMMTensorReference],
+    max_nbytes: int,
+) -> int:
+    """Check and return the total declared size of one request's objects."""
+    nbytes = sum(reference.nbytes for reference in references)
+    if nbytes > max_nbytes:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Multimodal tensor objects in one request declare {nbytes} bytes, "
+            f"exceeding the configured limit of {max_nbytes} bytes"
+        )
+    return nbytes
+
+
+class MMTensorReservation:
+    """Bytes reserved from an `MMTensorMemoryBudget`, returned by the last holder."""
+
+    def __init__(self, budget: "MMTensorMemoryBudget", nbytes: int) -> None:
+        self._budget = budget
+        self._nbytes = nbytes
+        self._holders = 1
+
+    def hold(self) -> None:
+        self._holders += 1
+
+    def release(self) -> None:
+        self._holders -= 1
+        if self._holders == 0:
+            self._budget._release(self._nbytes)
+
+
+class MMTensorMemoryBudget:
+    """Bytes one API server may hold for referenced multimodal tensors.
+
+    Requests wait in arrival order until their reservation fits. All methods
+    must be called from the event loop thread.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, max_nbytes: int) -> None:
+        self.max_nbytes = max_nbytes
+        self.used_nbytes = 0
+        self._waiters: deque[tuple[int, asyncio.Future[None]]] = deque()
+
+    async def reserve(self, nbytes: int) -> MMTensorReservation:
+        if nbytes > self.max_nbytes:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Reserving {nbytes} bytes for multimodal tensors exceeds "
+                f"max_reserved_bytes ({self.max_nbytes})"
+            )
+        if not self._waiters and self.used_nbytes + nbytes <= self.max_nbytes:
+            self.used_nbytes += nbytes
+            return MMTensorReservation(self, nbytes)
+
+        waiter = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
+        self._waiters.append((nbytes, waiter))
+        try:
+            await waiter
+        except asyncio.CancelledError:
+            if waiter.done() and not waiter.cancelled():
+                # Granted just before the cancellation.
+                self._release(nbytes)
+            else:
+                self._wake()
+            raise
+        return MMTensorReservation(self, nbytes)
+
+    def _release(self, nbytes: int) -> None:
+        self.used_nbytes -= nbytes
+        self._wake()
+
+    def _wake(self) -> None:
+        while self._waiters:
+            nbytes, waiter = self._waiters[0]
+            if waiter.done():
+                self._waiters.popleft()
+            elif self.used_nbytes + nbytes <= self.max_nbytes:
+                self._waiters.popleft()
+                self.used_nbytes += nbytes
+                waiter.set_result(None)
+            else:
+                break
+
+
+class ReleasingStream(AsyncIterator[_T]):
+    """Iterate `stream` and release `reservations` once it's done with.
+
+    That's when the stream ends or fails, when it's closed, or when it's
+    dropped without ever being iterated, which an async generator's
+    `finally` would miss.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        stream: AsyncGenerator[_T, None],
+        reservations: Iterable[MMTensorReservation],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._stream = stream
+        self._release = weakref.finalize(
+            self,
+            _release_soon,
+            asyncio.get_running_loop(),
+            tuple(reservations),
+        )
+
+    def __aiter__(self) -> "ReleasingStream[_T]":
+        return self
+
+    async def __anext__(self) -> _T:
+        try:
+            return await self._stream.__anext__()
+        except BaseException:
+            self._release()
+            raise
+
+    async def aclose(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            await self._stream.aclose()
+        finally:
+            self._release()
+
+
+def _release_soon(
+    loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, reservations: tuple[MMTensorReservation, ...]
+) -> None:
+    # A finalizer can run on any thread; the budget belongs to the loop's.
+    def release() -> None:
+        for reservation in reservations:
+            reservation.release()
+
+    with contextlib.suppress(RuntimeError):  # The loop has closed.
+        loop.call_soon_threadsafe(release)
+
+
+async def run_in_read_slot(
+    semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore,
+    fn: Callable[[], _T],
+    reservation: MMTensorReservation | None = None,
+    executor: Executor | None = None,
+) -> _T:
+    """Run `fn` in `executor` while holding a slot of `semaphore`.
+
+    The slot, and a hold on `reservation`, are released only when `fn`
+    returns, even if the caller is cancelled first, because the executor
+    thread keeps running.
+    """
+    await semaphore.acquire()
+    try:
+        future = asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(executor, fn)
+    except BaseException:
+        semaphore.release()
+        raise
+    if reservation is not None:
+        reservation.hold()
+
+    def release(done: asyncio.Future[_T]) -> None:
+        semaphore.release()
+        if reservation is not None:
+            reservation.release()
+        if not done.cancelled():
+            # Mark the exception retrieved when the caller was cancelled.
+            done.exception()
+
+    future.add_done_callback(release)
+    return await asyncio.shield(future)
+
+
+def verify_mm_tensor_digest(payload: bytes, expected_digest: str) -> bool:
+    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() == expected_digest
+
+
+def decode_mm_tensor_bundle(
+    payload: bytes, *, location: str
+) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Decode one SafeTensors bundle whose digest has been verified."""
+    try:
+        tensors = load_safetensors(payload)
+    except Exception as e:
+        raise MMTensorTransportError(
+            f"Could not decode multimodal tensor object {location} "
+            f"as {MM_TENSOR_FORMAT}"
+        ) from e
+    if not tensors:
+        raise MMTensorTransportError(
+            f"Multimodal tensor object {location} contains no tensors"
+        )
+    return tensors

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""QSA prefill attention with FlashInfer's QToken-KvBlock-Sparse kernel.
+
+It attends GROUP_SIZE rows of a request as one tile over the union of their
+selected blocks, so each K/V block is read once per group rather than per row.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.utils.flashinfer import has_flashinfer
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv, next_power_of_2
+
+# Query rows per FlashInfer route, the best on Qwen3.8 prefill shapes.
+GROUP_SIZE = 8
+
+
+def is_flashinfer_qsa_supported(
+    kv_dtype: torch.dtype,
+    block_size: int,
+    block_topk: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether FlashInfer 0.7.4 can plan this geometry on this device."""
+    return (
+        current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+        and kv_dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and has_flashinfer()
+        and block_size in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128)
+        and head_dim in (64, 128, 192, 256)
+        and block_topk <= 512
+        # A tile holds GROUP_SIZE rows x the query heads of one KV head.
+        and GROUP_SIZE * (num_heads // num_kv_heads) <= 128
+    )
+
+
+def get_workspace_size(
+    max_num_tokens: int,
+    max_num_reqs: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    page_size: int,
+    max_seq_len_kv: int,
+    block_size: int,
+    block_topk: int,

+    kv_cache_ptr,

+    seq_lens_ptr,
+    stride_block,
+    stride_head,
+    stride_token,
+    stride_table,
+    PAGE_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_KV_HEADS: tl.constexpr,

+    ROW_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    KV_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,

+    block_end = (seq_len + KV_BLOCK - 1) // KV_BLOCK * KV_BLOCK

+                    tl.zeros([ROW_BLOCK], dtype=kv_cache_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+                    mask=cols < ROW,

+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    launch_pdl: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    offsets = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < numel
+    if launch_pdl:
+        tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()

+    gate = tl.load(gate_ptr + offsets, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    if launch_pdl:
+        tl.extra.cuda.gdc_launch_dependents()

+        output_ptr + offsets,
+        output.to(tl.float32) * tl.sigmoid(gate.to(tl.float32)),

+def qsa_sparse_paged_prefill(
+    query: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,

+    block_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    token_to_req: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    qo_indptr: torch.Tensor,
+    block_size: int,

+    out: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """Write `sigmoid(output_gate) * attention` of prefill rows into `out`.
+
+    `block_indices` holds the indexer's selected blocks, -1 padded;
+    `token_to_req` indexes all of `block_table`, whose prefill requests start
+    at `num_decodes`; `seq_lens` holds those requests' lengths.
+    """
+    from flashinfer.attention.prims_ts import QTokenKvBlockSparsePagedTSWrapper
+
+    _, num_kv_heads, page_size, row = kv_cache.shape
+    head_dim = row // 2
+    k_cache, v_cache = kv_cache[..., :head_dim], kv_cache[..., head_dim:]
+    # FlashInfer loads whole blocks and its causal mask does not clear NaN/Inf
+    # in V; unwritten tail slots may hold another cache group's bytes.
+    _zero_partial_tail_kernel[(seq_lens.numel(),)](
+        kv_cache,
+        block_table[num_decodes:],
+        seq_lens,
+        kv_cache.stride(0),
+        kv_cache.stride(1),
+        kv_cache.stride(2),
+        block_table.stride(0),
+        PAGE_SIZE=page_size,
+        NUM_KV_HEADS=num_kv_heads,
+        ROW=row,
+        ROW_BLOCK=next_power_of_2(row),
+        KV_BLOCK=block_size,
+    )
+    workspace = torch.empty(workspace_size, dtype=torch.uint8, device=query.device)
+    # A plan binds this layer's K/V and the batch shapes, so plan every call;
+    # its ~0.35 ms of host time hides behind the GPU except on short prefills.
+    # TODO: fix in FlashInfer (bind K/V and shapes per run()) and plan once.
+    wrapper = QTokenKvBlockSparsePagedTSWrapper()
+    wrapper.plan(
+        qo_indptr.numel() - 1,
+        query.shape[1],
+        num_kv_heads,
+        head_dim,
+        block_size,
+        page_size,
+        block_indices.shape[1],
+        max_seq_len_kv,
+        device=query.device,
+        workspace_buffer=workspace,
+        group_size=GROUP_SIZE,
+        packed_query=True,
+        split_kv=False,
+        q_dtype=query.dtype,
+    )
+    wrapper.run(
+        query,
+        (k_cache, v_cache),
+        block_table,
+        block_indices,
+        token_to_req,
+        positions,
+        qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
+        sm_scale=scale,
+        out=out,
+    )
+    numel = out.numel()
+    BLOCK = 2048
+    _sigmoid_gate_mul_kernel[(triton.cdiv(numel, BLOCK),)](
+        out,
+        output_gate,
+        numel,
+        BLOCK=BLOCK,
+        launch_pdl=current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl(),
+        num_warps=4,
+    )

+"""Full-head attention sinks for HY4 ShardQ prefill."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group

+
+def gather_full_sinks_(sinks: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor | None) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """All-gather this rank's sinks into `out` across TP.
+
+    `out` is filled in place, so captured graphs read reloaded sinks. It is
+    allocated on the first call, when `out` is None.
+    """
+    tp_group = get_tp_group()
+    full = tp_group.all_gather(sinks.to(tp_group.device), dim=0)
+    if out is None:
+        out = torch.empty_like(full)
+    out.copy_(full)
+    return out
